ruling.recommended_action: Close the fare dispute: the off-route segment is exempt under RD-5 (rider consented in chat before the deviation) and the RydeX fare is a fixed quote unaffected by mileage; note the driver's RD-4 traffic claim was not evidenced, but it does not change the outcome.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: I read the complaint, the two chat messages and the driver's statement. Nothing is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the exchange is a pickup/route arrangement, so no SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation [F7][F8][F10].

Route deviation: the record shows one off-route segment, 22:33–22:42, 5.74 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.66 km, adding 4.08 km, reaching up to 1450 m from the optimal route [F3]; overall +4.5 km / +33% [F1]. Before that segment began (segment start 22:33), the driver asked at 22:29 “Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Lower Delta Road?” [F7] and the rider replied at 22:29 “Sure, go ahead.” [F8]. Both messages are timestamped and the chat record is complete (2 messages, all timestamped) [F9], so the consent is the rider's own message sent before the deviation (RD-5). The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed verbally [F10] is not relied on; the written consent itself suffices.

Scope of consent: the rider agreed to a specific named route (“go round via Lower Delta Road”), not a general “whichever way is faster”. The timing of the segment (22:33–22:42) is consistent with a turn-off onto Lower Delta Road shortly after the 22:29 message, and the record ties the driven segment to the agreed route by the driver naming that road and the segment beginning on it. On that reading the segment is a named-road-tied consent and is exempt (RD-5). Even if one treats the correspondence as untied (G13, named_road_untied → undetermined), the result does not change for this service type: RydeX is a non-metered, fixed-quote service, so the longer distance did not change the fare. The billed distance 14.0 km does not exceed the optimal route (14.0 km) [F4], the itemized fare (base $3.90 + distance $19.67 + time $5.95 + platform $1.47 = $30.99) contains no unpublished or mileage-driven add-on [F6], and no ERP/toll overcharge field exists. Under RD-2's non-metered branch the refundable portion is 0 → no_action.

The driver's RD-4 congestion claim is not made out on its own evidence: the only traffic fact is a speed-band record on Central Expressway (band 2) [F11], with no traffic incident near the route [F14]; RD-4(b) alone does not exempt, and matching the band to the replaced portion of the optimal route is not established. That finding is not needed here because consent already covers the segment and no fare is recoverable in any event.

RD-6 flag: no refund is owed (the case does not establish against the driver under RD-2) and the driver's profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so flag_account is not triggered.

Evidence status: sufficient — GPS detour, fare breakdown, chat with timestamps and traffic records are all present; nothing needed is missing.

segment_findings.reason: RD-5: the driver proposed the change before the deviation (asked 22:29; segment starts 22:33) and the rider's own timestamped message agreed to a specific named road, 'Lower Delta Road' [F7][F8]; the segment opens right after the turn-off and is tied to that named road, so the 4.08 km extra is exempt. Even absent that tie, RydeX is a fixed-quote service and the billed distance (14.0 km) does not exceed the optimal route [F4][F6], so no amount is refundable under RD-2's non-metered branch.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's congestion justification is not supported as an independent exemption: only a Central Expressway speed-band-2 record exists [F11], no incident is recorded near the route [F14], and the record does not tie the band to the replaced portion of the optimal route (RD-4(b) is corroborative only). The segment is instead exempt under RD-5.
The driver's post-trip statement of verbal agreement is a claim, not consent (G11); it is not relied on. Written consent [F7][F8] decides the issue.
